title: Bounded local acyclic monomorphisms detect all local lifting problems
statement: Fix a universe of small sets and the category $\mathrm{sS}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{sSet})$, Reedy model structure and simplicial mapping sets of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. Let $f:P\hookrightarrow Q$ be a monomorphism in $\mathrm{sS}$. Call $Z$ local if it is Reedy fibrant and $\operatorname{Map}(Q,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(P,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $T_f$ be the class of monomorphisms $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ for which $\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every local $Z$. For a class $E$ of arrows, write $E^{\square}$ for the arrows with the right diagonal-lifting property against every member of $E$, as defined in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. There is an uncountable small cardinal $\gamma$ such that, if $J_\gamma$ is any set of representatives of the isomorphism classes of arrows $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ in $T_f$ with $\left|\coprod_{p,q\geq0}B_{p,q}\right|<\gamma$, then $J_\gamma^{\square}=T_f^{\square}$. An isomorphism of arrows means a commutative square with invertible source and target maps. The cardinal $\gamma$ may depend on $f$, and is not asserted to be countable or independent of $P,Q$.

source.place: Rezk, A model for the homotopy theory of homotopy theory, Proposition 9.1 proof, final paragraph, printed p. 22: Bousfield-Smith bound for the generating local trivial cofibration. Replacing a degreewise bound by a total bound is harmless after increasing the uncountable cardinal. Read online; WANTED in report.md; no Stacks tag for this result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-bousfield-smith-bounded-generation] to $f$ and fix its uncountable regular cardinal $\gamma$. Up to isomorphism there is a small set of simplicial spaces of total size $<\gamma$: replace every bidegree set by an ordinal less than $\gamma$; the countable list of these sets and their structure functions ranges over a small set. The subspaces of each such target also form a small set of bidegreewise subsets. Consequently the bounded monomorphisms have a small set of arrow-isomorphism representatives. The property defining $T_f$ is invariant under arrow isomorphism, since precomposition by isomorphisms gives inverse isomorphisms on mapping simplicial sets. Choose any representatives $J_\gamma$ of the bounded members of $T_f$.

source.place: Proposition 9.1 final paragraph: bounded representatives; the cardinal with bounded-subobject property is the separately stated Hirschhorn input.

proof.text: For each local $Z$ and $n\geq0$ let $r_{Z,n}:Z^{c\Delta^n}\to Z^{c\partial\Delta^n}$ be restriction, using the constant simplicial spaces and internal hom of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. Let $S$ be the class of these maps. If $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ is monic, then $\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$ is a Kan fibration: apply the mapping-fibration assertion of that node to $i$ and $Z\to1$. It is a weak equivalence exactly when it is a trivial fibration. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], this is equivalent to lifting every $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. Such a square is a compatible pair of maps $B\times c\partial\Delta^n\to Z$ and $A\times c\Delta^n\to Z$; its filler is a map $B\times c\Delta^n\to Z$. By the internal-hom definition these are exactly the squares and fillers for $i$ against $r_{Z,n}$. Thus $T_f$ is precisely the monomorphisms in ${}^{\square}S$, with lifting notation as in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure].

source.place: Agent expansion of the simplicial mapping-space test used in Proposition 9.1; no localized model structure is used.

proof.text: It follows that $T_f$ contains identities and is closed under pushouts, binary composition and small continuous transfinite compositions. For the lifting condition apply [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] and, for transfinite compositions, [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] to the class $S$ of Step 2; neither result assumes that $S$ is a set. For monomorphisms, compute a pushout of an injection in each bidegree as the disjoint union modulo its specified identifications, in which the other summand still injects. A chain of injections identifies with an increasing union in each bidegree, so its transfinite composite is injective. These degreewise constructions inherit the simplicial operators and satisfy the colimit universal property by gluing compatible functions. Also, the class $W_f$ of all $f$-local equivalences satisfies two-out-of-three: precomposition takes a composite to the composite of the two maps of mapping simplicial sets, and weak equivalences in the Kan model structure satisfy two-out-of-three by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and the model-category axioms in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure].

source.place: Agent expansion of the closure properties needed for the Bousfield–Smith filtration.

proof.text: Fix $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ in $T_f$ and identify $A$ with its image. Well-order the small total set of simplices of $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem], and enumerate it $(b_\alpha)_{\alpha<\theta}$ by its small ordinal order type. Use [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] to construct increasing subspaces $E_\alpha\subseteq B$ for $\alpha\leq\theta$, with $E_0=A$ and unions at nonzero limits. The induction invariant is that $A\hookrightarrow E_\alpha$ belongs to $T_f$ and that $E_\alpha\hookrightarrow B$ is an $f$-local equivalence. It holds at zero since $i\in T_f$. At a successor, the subspace $C_\alpha$ generated by $b_\alpha$ is countable: all its elements are images of this simplex under pairs of simplex-category maps, and there are only countably many such maps. Hence $|C_\alpha|<\gamma$. Apply [lem-coef-bousfield-smith-bounded-generation] to $E_\alpha\hookrightarrow B$ and $C_\alpha$, obtaining $D_\alpha\subseteq B$ with $b_\alpha\in D_\alpha$, $|D_\alpha|<\gamma$ and $j_\alpha:E_\alpha\cap D_\alpha\hookrightarrow D_\alpha$ in $T_f$. Put $E_{\alpha+1}=E_\alpha\cup D_\alpha$. The successor inclusion is the pushout of $j_\alpha$ along $E_\alpha\cap D_\alpha\hookrightarrow E_\alpha$, as seen by gluing functions on the two subsets. Step 3 gives $A\hookrightarrow E_{\alpha+1}\in T_f$, and two-out-of-three with $A\hookrightarrow B$ gives $E_{\alpha+1}\hookrightarrow B\in W_f$. At a nonzero limit, Step 3 applies to the preceding continuous chain and gives $A\hookrightarrow E_\beta\in T_f$; the same two-out-of-three gives the second invariant. Choices of $D_\alpha$ can be fixed by well-ordering the small set of subspaces of $B$ and taking the least eligible one; thus the rule used for recursion is defined. On incoherent prefixes use $A$ as a fallback; the verified induction shows this fallback never occurs. At the end, every enumerated simplex is in $E_{\alpha+1}$, so $E_\theta=B$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the Bousfield–Smith argument: bounded intersection enlargement followed by an explicit successor and limit induction.

proof.text: Each $j_\alpha$ in Step 4 has target of total size $<\gamma$ and belongs to $T_f$, so it is arrow-isomorphic to a member of $J_\gamma$. Fix $p\in J_\gamma^{\square}$. A square for $j_\alpha$ against $p$ can be precomposed by its chosen arrow isomorphism, filled using $p\in J_\gamma^{\square}$, and transported back by the inverse isomorphism; the two filler identities follow by composing the inverse maps. Thus every $j_\alpha$ has the left lifting property against $p$. Its pushout $E_\alpha\to E_{\alpha+1}$ does too by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. The chain is continuous, so [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting], applied to $T=\{p\}$, gives the left lifting property of $A=E_0\to E_\theta=B$ against $p$. As $i$ was arbitrary, this proves $J_\gamma^{\square}\subseteq T_f^{\square}$. This argument uses single pushouts, with no coproduct-closure assertion.

source.place: Proposition 9.1 final paragraph, bounded generators detect all local lifting problems; closure inputs are now cited in their exact strength.

proof.text: Conversely $J_\gamma\subseteq T_f$, so every member of $T_f^{\square}$ lifts against each member of $J_\gamma$ by the definition of the right lifting class [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Hence $T_f^{\square}\subseteq J_\gamma^{\square}$, and together with Step 5 this gives the asserted equality for any choice of representatives.

lean.statement: theorem bounded_local_lifting {P Q : SimplicialSpace.{u}} (f : P ⟶ Q) (_hf : Mono f) : ∃ γ : Cardinal.{u}, Cardinal.aleph0 < γ ∧ ∀ (Jγ : Set (Arrow SimplicialSpace.{u})), (∀ a : Arrow SimplicialSpace.{u}, a ∈ Jγ → localAcyclicMonomorphisms f a.hom ∧ Cardinal.mk (Σ p q : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, (a.right.obj p).obj q) < γ) ∧ (∀ a : Arrow SimplicialSpace.{u}, localAcyclicMonomorphisms f a.hom → Cardinal.mk (Σ p q : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, (a.right.obj p).obj q) < γ → ∃ b : Arrow SimplicialSpace.{u}, b ∈ Jγ ∧ Nonempty (a ≅ b)) ∧ (∀ a b : Arrow SimplicialSpace.{u}, a ∈ Jγ → b ∈ Jγ → Nonempty (a ≅ b) → a = b) → (fun _ _ p ↦ ∀ a : Arrow SimplicialSpace.{u}, a ∈ Jγ → HasLiftingProperty a.hom p) = (localAcyclicMonomorphisms f).rlp
